newsitem.title: USA: Ford Credit Chairman, CEO Odom to retire.
newsitem.headline: Ford Credit Chairman, CEO Odom to retire.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Thursday Bill Odom will retire as chairman and chief executive officer of Ford Credit, the automaker's primary finance arm.
Ken Whipple, who is president of Ford's Financial Services Group, which oversees Ford Credit, will take over Odom's titles, the company said.
Edsell Ford II will continue as president and chief operating officer of Ford Credit, the company said.
Odom, 61, joined Ford Credit in 1966 in its Diversified Financing Operations. He has been chairman of the company since October 1987. Odom's retirement is effective March 1.
Ford Credit spokesman Della DiPietro said he is leaving to travel and spend more time with his family.
"This truly was Bill's choice," she said. "Bill is looking forward to retirement. He asked for this timing."
Odom's departure comes after a major restructuring of Ford's Financial Services Group last year.
FSG sold 20 percent of its Associates First Capital Corp stock in a public offering last year. Ford has also been selling the business units of its USL Capital subsidiary.
In a statement, Ford Chairman Alex Trotman said the company decided to not hire a new replacement for Odom to cut a management rank.
"We're taking the opportunity of his retirement and the restructuring of our financial services business to eliminate a layer of management structure," he said.
DiPietro said no other changes are planned at Ford Credit.

Whipple, who has been with Ford for 38 years, has previously worked for Ford Credit and served as its president from 1980-84. Whipple plans to retain his office at Ford World Headquarters and as well as work from Odom's old office in the nearby Ford Credit headquarters.
"He will be dividing his time between his office at Ford Credit and his offices at Ford World Headquarters," DiPietro said.
